articles.title: Fauci Perjury File: Rand Paul Demands DOJ Investigate Whether America's COVID Czar Lied to Congress About Gain-of-Function Funding
articles.summary: Senator Rand Paul has formally referred Dr. Anthony Fauci to the Department of Justice for alleged perjury during 2021 congressional testimony, asserting Fauci knowingly misled Congress when he denied NIH funding of gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. If proven, this would mean the architect of America's COVID response committed federal crimes to conceal the origins of the pandemic. The DOJ has so far declined to act — itself a story worth telling.

articles.title: Fauci's Own Diary Exposes the Man Behind the Mask: Trump Contempt, China Praise, and Classified Files Lost in a Ransomware Hack
articles.summary: Newly released diary pages from Dr. Anthony Fauci reveal a figure who privately disparaged the sitting U.S. president while lavishing praise on Chinese health officials — the same officials who stonewalled a transparent pandemic investigation. The diary also confirms Fauci lost a set of confidential records in a ransomware hack, raising serious questions about information security and what those files contained. This is the unfiltered Fauci the press refused to show you for four years.

articles.title: The Antidepressant Reckoning: What the Science Actually Shows About Benefits, Harms, and a Nation Hooked on Pills
articles.summary: A rigorous examination of the antidepressant evidence base reveals a medication class prescribed to tens of millions whose mechanisms remain poorly understood and whose harm profile — including dependence, sexual dysfunction, and withdrawal — is routinely minimized by prescribers. The chemical imbalance theory that sold a generation on SSRIs has been quietly walked back by its own proponents, yet prescriptions continue to climb. The gap between what doctors tell patients and what the data shows is a scandal hiding in plain sight.

articles.title: Off-Patent, Cheap, and Effective: Why Dr. Makis Says Repurposed Drugs Like Ivermectin Could Upend Cancer Care — and Why Oncology Won't Touch Them
articles.summary: Canadian physician Dr. William Makis is making the case that inexpensive, off-patent drugs including ivermectin show genuine mechanistic and clinical signals against multiple cancer types — signals the profit-driven oncology establishment has no financial incentive to pursue. Peer-reviewed literature supports plausible anti-tumor activity, yet no major cancer center is running the trials. When a drug can't be patented, patients don't get the research — that is pharma capture in its purest form.

articles.title: Medical Device Maker Beta Bionics Accused of Hiding Safety Failures From Investors — FDA Compliance Problems Trigger Securities Fraud Lawsuit
articles.summary: Beta Bionics, maker of the iLet automated insulin delivery device, now faces a securities fraud class action after its stock collapsed more than 37% when undisclosed FDA compliance and safety issues became public. Investors allege company executives knowingly misrepresented the device's safety record and commercial trajectory while the problems mounted. When medical device companies hide safety data from markets, patients and investors both pay the price.

articles.title: Repurposed Cancer Drug Mebendazole Suppresses Gefitinib-Resistant Lung Tumors — Science Big Pharma Won't Fund Because It Costs Pennies
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed study in PLOS ONE demonstrates that mebendazole, a decades-old antiparasitic costing cents per dose, disrupts microtubule dynamics and significantly suppresses tumor growth in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer — one of oncology's most lethal dead ends. The mechanism is biologically coherent and the results are striking, yet no pharmaceutical company will fund the trials needed to bring this to patients because there is no patent revenue to capture. Science that saves lives but makes no money gets buried.

articles.title: COVID Testing Clinics Billed the Government $20 Million for Fake Office Visits — The Pandemic Fraud Nobody Wanted to Prosecute
articles.summary: Heal 360 clinics in Plano, Texas have agreed to pay $20 million to settle federal allegations that they systematically billed nasal swab COVID tests as full office visits, defrauding pandemic relief programs designed for the uninsured. This is one node in a vast ecosystem of COVID-era billing fraud that federal investigators have only scratched the surface of — enabled by emergency authorizations that stripped normal oversight and created a feeding frenzy at taxpayer expense.

articles.title: Epstein Whistleblower Who Exposed Commerce Secretary Lutnick's Ties Dies by 'Suicide' — Investigators and the Public Demand Answers

articles.title: Antidepressants: The Harm Data Big Psychiatry Doesn't Want You to Read

The review arrives as prescribing rates continue to climb globally, with regulatory agencies consistently downplaying harm signals in favor of industry-friendly efficacy narratives. Critics argue the informed consent process for these drugs remains fundamentally broken.
